messages:
leah-peopleops: Hey team — new hire married in Canada and uploaded a bilingual marriage certificate (English/French) but no apostille. They asked if that's sufficient for spouse enrollment or if we need extra verification.
tom-benefits: Canada is unlike many countries; no apostille system. A stamped copy from the provincial vital stats office + certified translation (if not already bilingual) usually works. Which province?
leah-peopleops: Ontario — doc is an official PDF from ServiceOntario, bilingual header.
tom-benefits: That should generally be fine. Ask the employee to attach the source URL/printout showing the certificate came from ServiceOntario and upload it to the Benefits Portal. If the file is clearly an official PDF with government header we accept it.
sri-payroll: Quick payroll note: if they want pre-tax deductions to start immediately we need to either have SSN/ITIN or the employee signs the provisional attestation so payroll codes deductions correctly. We can backdate enrollments to the QLE date, but tax/withholding depends on SSN/ITIN presence.
leah-peopleops: Got it. If the system flags it, can Benefits mark as verified so payroll can proceed?
tom-benefits: Yes — once I review the doc I can mark it Verified in the portal. If anything looks off I'll request certified translation.
leah-peopleops: Awesome. Any special handling for domestic partner classification vs spouse?
omelia-hr: (typo) — olivia-hr: For US plan rules, if marriage is legally recognized in the country of marriage and supported by documentation, we treat them as spouse for benefits eligibility. Domestic partner is a separate attestation process; do not change classification unless employee requests DP instead.
leah-peopleops: Thanks — I'll send the checklist to the new hire.
emma-hrbot: Reminder: QLE documentation must be uploaded within 30 days to avoid coverage gaps. See policy: https://intranet.redwood/benefits/qle.
sri-payroll: If verification takes longer than 30 days we can extend coverage temporarily on case-by-case basis but payroll needs a signed attestation and case note. Tag me @sri-payroll if you need an extension.
tom-benefits: Copying verification steps for the hire: 
1) Go to Benefits Portal > Documents > Add Dependent
2) Upload ServiceOntario PDF (or equivalent government source) + any translations if required
3) Add supporting URL/screenshot proving origin
4) Add SSN/ITIN when available
5) In notes, include "QLE - provisionally enrolled pending verification"
leah-peopleops: Sending now. Will tag you both when they reply. :white_check_mark:
